definitions.explanation: A formal rule or provision established by law, contract, or organization. Also used as a する verb meaning to stipulate or prescribe.

examples.japanese: {法律|ほうりつ}の{規定|きてい}に{従|したが}う。
examples.english: I follow the provisions of the law.

examples.japanese: {就業|しゅうぎょう}{規定|きてい}では{残業|ざんぎょう}は{月|つき}30{時間|じかん}までだ。
examples.english: The work regulations limit overtime to 30 hours per month.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}に{規定|きてい}されていない{事項|じこう}については、{別途|べっと}{協議|きょうぎ}する。
examples.english: Matters not stipulated in the contract will be discussed separately.

notes:
USAGE:
{規定|きてい} refers to specific rules or clauses within a larger system of regulations. Compare with {規則|きそく} (rules in general, often for everyday conduct), {法律|ほうりつ} (law), and {規約|きやく} (terms, bylaws). {規定|きてい} tends to appear in formal and legal contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {規定|きてい}に{従|したが}う: to follow regulations
- {規定|きてい}を{設|もう}ける: to establish a regulation
- {規定|きてい}{違反|いはん}: violation of a regulation
- {規定|きてい}どおり: as prescribed/stipulated
- {服務|ふくむ}{規定|きてい}: service regulations
